issues.legal_issue: A claimant may amend a timely compensation reference to increase the amount claimed, and the limitation period for seeking a reference does not apply to that amendment.
material_facts: The landowner timely sought a reference objecting to the amount of compensation and stated a lower amount of compensation sought.
During the reference proceedings, the landowner sought to increase the compensation claim and paid the additional court fee.
The Reference Court allowed the amendment.
issues.conclusion: A claimant who timely seeks a reference objecting to the amount of compensation may later amend the compensation claim to seek a higher amount; the limitation period for seeking the reference does not bar that amendment.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 18 and 19 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, the claimant must timely identify the nature and grounds of the objection, but need not specify the amount of compensation claimed. The limitation period governs seeking the reference, not specifying or increasing the compensation claim before the Reference Court. The reference is an original proceeding in which compensation is determined afresh under section 23, not an appeal from the Collector’s offer: Chimanlal Hargovinddas v. Special Land Acquisition Officer, Poona. Amendments are considered under the general principles of Order 6 Rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure, as recognized in State of Maharashtra v. Sitaram Narayan Patil.

predicates.land_acquisition_reference: A claimant is pursuing a reference to have compensation for acquired property determined by a court.
predicates.timely_objection_to_compensation: The claimant timely objected to the amount of compensation and sought a reference.
predicates.later_increase_in_compensation_claim: The claimant later sought a higher amount of compensation in the reference proceedings.

issues.definition: When a claimant timely seeks a reference objecting to compensation and later asks for a higher amount, the later increase is not barred by the time limit for seeking the reference.

issues.legal_issue: A claimant who referred an objection to the amount of compensation may seek increased compensation for trees or structures even if the original reference application sought an increase only for the land.
material_facts: The landowner’s timely reference objected to the amount of compensation and sought an increase for the land, but not for the trees or well.
During the reference proceedings, the landowner sought increased compensation for the trees and well as well as the land.
The acquired property included land, fruit-bearing trees, and a well.
issues.conclusion: Once a reference is made objecting to the amount of compensation, the claimant may seek increased compensation for the land, trees, structures, and other appurtenances; the original application need not separately identify each component for which an increase is sought.
issues.legal_principle: Section 18 permits an objection to the amount of compensation without requiring the claimant to specify the amount sought or each component for which an increase is claimed. Under section 3(a), “land” includes benefits arising from land and things attached to the earth. Sections 18 and 19, read together, give the Reference Court jurisdiction to determine compensation for the acquired land and its appurtenances. The limitation period prevents changing the category of objection after it expires, but not adding or increasing claims under the compensation objection. The general approach to amendment is also reflected in State of Maharashtra v. Sitaram Narayan Patil.

predicates.land_acquisition_reference: A claimant is pursuing a reference to have compensation for acquired property determined by a court.
predicates.timely_objection_to_compensation: The claimant timely objected to the amount of compensation and sought a reference.
predicates.later_claim_for_another_property_compone: The claimant later sought increased compensation for a component of the acquired property that was not separately identified in the original application.

issues.definition: If a claimant timely refers an objection to the amount of compensation and later seeks compensation for another acquired component, the court may consider compensation for all acquired components.

issues.legal_issue: Separate compensation for trees is not categorically barred when compensation is also awarded for the acquired land, but the value of trees cannot be counted twice.
material_facts: The acquired land included fruit-bearing trees.
The land value was determined by reference to vacant agricultural land, not an orchard or the yield from the trees.
The trees’ value had not been included in the land valuation.
issues.conclusion: The value of the trees could be added to the value of the land in these circumstances. Separate tree compensation is not permissible where the land value already reflects an orchard or has been determined by capitalizing yield.
issues.legal_principle: Section 3(a) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 includes things attached to the earth within “land.” State of Haryana v. Gurcharan Singh does not establish an absolute bar on separate valuation of fruit-bearing trees: where land value is based on vacant-land comparables, tree value may be added; where it is based on orchard comparables or capitalized yield, adding tree value separately would duplicate compensation.

rule.if: land_acquisition_compensation_proceeding and acquired_land_has_trees and land_value_based_on_vacant_land and tree_value_not_included_in_land_value

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_proceeding: A court is determining compensation for land acquired by the government.
predicates.acquired_land_has_trees: The acquired land includes trees whose value is in issue.
predicates.land_value_based_on_vacant_land: The land value was determined using vacant-land comparisons rather than orchard comparisons or capitalized yield.
predicates.tree_value_not_included_in_land_value: The value of the trees was not already included in the land valuation.

issues.definition: When acquired land has trees and the land valuation neither uses orchard or yield value nor includes the trees’ value, separate tree compensation may be added.
